Level 1: Execution-Level & Language Safe.description: Base-level safety requirements that must be met at the EVM or compiler level, regardless of business logic.

1.1 Arithmetic Safety.description: Ensures numerical correctness under EVM constraints without unexpected mutations.

properties.name: Integer Overflow/Underflow
properties.invariant_template: unchecked { require(b == 0 || c / b == a); } // For multiplication
properties.description: Verify arithmetic operations in `unchecked` blocks to prevent wrap-around behavior.

properties.name: Division/Modulo by Zero
properties.description: Division by zero causes a Panic and transaction reversion.

properties.name: Precision Loss
properties.description: Ensure operation order follows 'multiply before divide' to prevent integer truncation.

properties.name: Casting Safety
properties.description: Check value ranges when downcasting (e.g., uint256 to uint8) to prevent silent truncation.

properties.name: Signed Integer Issues
properties.description: Prevent overflows when handling signed integers (e.g., INT_MIN / -1).

1.2 Resource & Memory Safety.description: Ensures the contract operates within limited computational resources (Gas, Stack, Memory).

properties.name: Out-of-Gas / Unbounded Loops
properties.description: Loops controlled by user input can exceed the Block Gas Limit, causing Denial of Service (DoS).

properties.name: Uninitialized Storage Pointers
properties.invariant_template: Struct memory s = Struct(x, y); // Explicit initialization
properties.description: Prevent uninitialized storage pointers from overwriting critical state variables (e.g., slot 0).

properties.name: Variable Shadowing
properties.description: Prevent local variables from shadowing state variables to avoid incorrect state updates.

1.3 Control Flow Integrity.description: Ensures execution paths are not hijacked, interrupted, or ignored unexpectedly.

properties.name: Re-entrancy Protection
properties.description: State changes must occur before external calls (CEI pattern), covering cross-function and read-only reentrancy.
properties.example_attack: The DAO Hack / Curve Read-only Reentrancy

properties.name: Unchecked Return Values
properties.description: Return values from low-level `.call()` must be checked to prevent silent failures.

properties.name: Unexpected Ether Handling
properties.description: Do not rely strictly on `address(this).balance` as `selfdestruct` can force Ether into the contract.

properties.name: Delegatecall Safety
properties.description: Storage layouts of the proxy and implementation contracts must match exactly.

1.4 Interface Compliance.description: Ensures the contract and its external interactions follow consistent communication protocols.

properties.name: ERC Standard Compliance
properties.description: Function parameters and return values must strictly adhere to EIP definitions.

properties.name: Non-Standard Token Compatibility
properties.description: Handle non-standard tokens (like USDT missing return values) using SafeERC20.

1.5 Environment Dependency Safety.description: Ensures secure usage of blockchain environment parameters.

properties.name: Timestamp Dependence
properties.description: `block.timestamp` can be manipulated by miners; do not use for precise randomness.

properties.name: Authorization via tx.origin
properties.description: Avoid `tx.origin` for authorization to prevent phishing/man-in-the-middle attacks.

Level 2: State Machine & Functional Corr.description: Focuses on state changes before/after function calls (Pre/Post-conditions), global invariants, and state machine transitions.

2.1 State Machine Integrity & Lifecycle.description: The contract must be viewed as a Finite State Machine (FSM) with closed and compliant transitions.

properties.name: Transition Validity & Irreversibility
properties.invariant_template: state == OLD_STATE implies next_state in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS
properties.description: States must transition according to a predefined directed graph; critical states (e.g., Active -> Fail) are irreversible.

properties.name: State Mutex
properties.description: Logically mutually exclusive states cannot be true simultaneously.

properties.name: Initialization & Finality
properties.description: Contracts must be initialized exactly once; critical state changes should stop in the final state.

2.2 Access Control.description: Validates operator eligibility, spatiotemporal snapshots, and permission attribution.

properties.name: Role Separation & Least Privilege
properties.description: Sensitive permissions should be separated to avoid single-point failure (admin rug pull).

properties.name: Eligibility Snapshots
properties.description: Permissions should depend on historical state (snapshots) rather than current state (to prevent flash loan attacks).

properties.name: Double-Action Prevention
properties.description: The same credential cannot be used twice in the same context (e.g., double voting).

2.3 Conservation & Isolation.description: Ensures conservation of asset/data totals and isolation between business domains.

properties.name: Solvency & Supply Conservation
properties.description: Contract assets must equal or exceed user liabilities; token transfers must be lossless.

properties.name: Business Logic Isolation
properties.description: Funds and states of different instances (e.g., in a Factory) must remain isolated.

2.4 Functional Correctness.description: Business logic complies with specifications, including math, conditions, and side effects.

properties.name: Pre/Post-conditions
properties.description: Assumptions before execution and state changes after execution must hold true.

properties.name: Side-effect Consistency
properties.description: On-chain state changes must be accompanied by correct Event emissions.

2.5 Input Validity & System Constraints.description: The system must operate within safe boundaries and reject abnormal inputs.

properties.name: Caps & Limits
properties.description: Enforce hard caps to prevent economic attacks (whale dominance) or system overflows.

properties.name: ID & Existence Checks
properties.description: Target objects (e.g., TokenIDs) must exist and be valid before operation.

Level 3: Temporal, Liveness & Interactio.description: Focuses on system evolution over time and interaction robustness in adversarial environments.

3.1 Liveness & Deadlock Freedom.description: The system must always advance to the next valid state and never permanently stall.

properties.name: Guaranteed Termination
properties.description: Processes (like auctions) must eventually end; no infinite loops in state.

properties.name: Guaranteed Withdrawal
properties.description: User funds must be withdrawable eventually, even if the admin absconds or the system pauses.

properties.name: Oracle Censorship Resistance
properties.description: Systems relying on oracles must have timeout/fallback mechanisms to prevent deadlock.
properties.example_attack: Frozen protocol due to Oracle failure

3.2 DoS Resistance & Interaction Isolati.description: Malicious behavior should not block other honest users or global processes.

properties.name: Push vs Pull Pattern
properties.description: Prioritize Pull (user withdraws) over Push (contract sends) to prevent DoS by malicious receivers.

properties.name: Forced Ether Defense
properties.description: Do not rely strictly on `address(this).balance` as `selfdestruct` can force Ether into the contract.

3.3 Temporal Constraints & Dynamic Adjus.description: Operation validity depends on on-chain time, and windows may adjust dynamically.

properties.name: Time Window Validity
properties.description: Operations outside the defined time window must be rejected.

properties.name: Dynamic Extension (Anti-Sniping)
properties.description: Interactions near the deadline should extend the window to ensure fairness.

3.4 Fairness & Race Condition Safety.description: Ensures transaction ordering does not cause severe unfairness in concurrent/high-latency environments.

properties.name: Front-running Protection
properties.description: Protect against MEV bots inserting transactions to profit (e.g., sandwich attacks).

properties.name: FIFO Fairness
properties.invariant_template: if (sold_out) revert(); // Late txs fail safely
properties.description: In limited resource scenarios, valid transactions before the cap is hit must succeed; late ones fail safely.

Level 4: Economic & Mechanism Design Saf.description: Verifies if the mechanism incentivizes honest behavior and prevents strategic attacks (Game Theory level).

4.1 Incentive Compatibility (IC).description: Designing mechanisms where honesty is the Dominant Strategy.

properties.name: Participation Incentive
properties.description: Incentives must cover gas and opportunity costs to prevent rational inaction by agents (e.g., Oracles).

properties.name: Slashing/Penalty Mechanism
properties.description: Verifiable malicious behavior must trigger on-chain economic penalties.

4.2 Strategy-Proofness & Manipulation Re.description: Preventing unfair gains through complex strategies (e.g., fake bids, multiple identities).

properties.name: Sybil Resistance
properties.description: The cost of creating fake identities must exceed the potential profit.

properties.name: Commitment Binding
properties.description: Users cannot dynamically change their decisions (e.g., bids) after committing to them.

4.3 Price Discovery & Market Efficiency.description: Ensures price curves reflect supply/demand correctly without risk-free arbitrage.

properties.name: Monotonicity & Convergence
properties.description: Price functions must change monotonically and converge to fair value.

properties.name: No Risk-Free Arbitrage
properties.description: There should be no risk-free arbitrage paths within the system.

4.4 Cooperative Game & Minority Protecti.description: Handling conflicts in collective decision-making and preventing 'tyranny of the majority'.

properties.name: Exit Right (Ragequit)
properties.description: Individuals must be able to exit with their funds if the collective decision violates their interests.

properties.name: Bribery Resistance
properties.description: Increase bribery costs (e.g., via vote locking) to exceed malicious profits.
